question.text: Half mole of an ideal monoatomic gas is heated at a constant pressure of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mtext> </mtext><mi>atm</mi></math> from <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo>°</mo><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>90</mn><mo>°</mo><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math>. Work done by the gas is<math><mo>(</mo></math>Gas constant,<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8.21</mn><mi> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi>mol</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>)

solution.text:
Recall the formula of work done in terms of change in volume and pressure, in the case of isobaric process, where pressure is constant, W=PV2-PV1, now take the idea of ideal gas equation, 
W=nRT2-nRT1=12×8.3170=291 J.
